description:
Who We Are

MOXFIVE helps enterprises respond to, recover from, and build resilience against cyber attacks. Our responders have led many of the most prominent security investigations in the world, from ransomware that takes a business offline to nation-state intrusions. When an attack hits, we work alongside the executives, outside counsel, and insurers who need answers fast and need answers they can defend.

The MOXFIVE founding team brings over 30 years of combined cybersecurity experience from leading companies such as CrowdStrike, Mandiant, Palo Alto Networks, Crypsis, Illumio, and Expel. Intelligent Insurer named MOXFIVE Cyber Security Consulting Team of the Year in 2024 and 2025, and Inc. has named us one of its Best Workplaces three times.

Today, we are focused on seizing an opportunity with the potential to disrupt the breach response market. We are building an AI investigation platform that puts our frontline experience behind every analyst on a case.

Who You Are

You are an engineer who treats agent behavior as a real engineering discipline, not prompt guesswork. You have shipped tool-using agents in production, dug through messy runs when they went sideways, and built evaluations that tell you whether a change actually helped.

You want to stay close to the full improvement loop. Rather than handing findings off to another team, you investigate why an agent fell short, test new approaches, and ship the changes directly into prompts, tools, and the runtime.

The Impact You'll Have

Our agents investigate real security incidents alongside forensic analysts, where every finding has to hold up under scrutiny. Because we are an active incident response firm, you will work directly with frontline responders rather than guessing on generic benchmarks.

You will design evaluations rooted in real-world tradecraft, research and test ways to make our agents sharper, and work alongside the team in the runtime to ship what proves out.
Your core responsibilities will include:

  • Investigation Evaluations: Building high-fidelity evaluation suites and realistic intrusion scenarios alongside forensic responders (including clean-host negative cases and tricky edge cases), calibrating automated graders against analyst judgment, and turning recurring failure modes into permanent regression tests.

  • Model Benchmarking & Selection: Evaluating frontier and specialized models, reasoning settings, and routing strategies against our forensic benchmarks to drive decisions on quality, latency, and cost.

  • Applied Agent Research: Investigating where our agents struggle on complex forensic workflows, researching new prompting, context, memory, and agent patterns, and running controlled experiments to separate real gains from noise.

  • Prompts, Tools & Runtime Iteration: Partnering directly in the agent runtime, system prompts, and tool interfaces (schemas, descriptions, context assembly, and error recovery) so evaluation insights land quickly in production.

  • Reliability & Safety Gates: Running evaluation checks before prompt, tool, model, or runtime changes ship, and testing how agents behave when reading adversarial or untrusted evidence.

What You'll Bring

  • Production Agent Engineering: You've built and operated tool-using LLM agents in production across multiple model providers, including multi-step control loops, tool calling, context management, and graceful failure handling.

  • Evaluation Systems: You've designed and maintained LLM evaluation harnesses in production (curated datasets, expert rubrics, automated judges calibrated to human reviewers, and CI regression suites), and you can talk candidly about where an eval misled you.

  • Trace-Driven Debugging: You can read a long agent trajectory, diagnose why the agent went off course, and turn messy qualitative failures into repeatable regression cases.

  • Strong Python: Production-grade Python with solid fundamentals in testing, observability, and maintainable system design, able to work directly in agent runtimes and build reliable evaluation tooling.

  • AI-Native Development: You build with coding agents every day and know how to review and verify what they produce.

  • Experimental & Measurement Rigor: You design clean model and prompt comparisons, separate real gains from run-to-run variance, and balance accuracy against latency and token cost.

  • Domain Collaboration: You work directly with subject-matter experts to translate tacit judgment into concrete rubrics and agent capabilities, and you communicate tradeoffs clearly in writing and in person.

Nice to Have

  • Security Domain: Experience building security products, or familiarity with digital forensics, incident response, or security telemetry.

  • Expert Domains: Experience building AI systems for specialists in high-stakes fields such as legal, healthcare, or finance where conclusions must be auditable.

  • Adversarial & Long-Horizon Agents: Experience hardening agents that inspect untrusted inputs (such as prompt-injection defenses) or operating long-running, stateful agent workflows.
